final_candidates.decision_summary: Surface-exposed loop position; lysine substitution maintains positive charge and may disrupt epitope for immune escape without core disruption.
Adjacent to R155 in antigenic region; glycine-to-aspartate introduces charge and potential steric hindrance to antibodies while tolerated in non-core site.
130-loop critical for receptor/antigen interaction; lysine preserves charge and modulates antigenic sites for escape with high folding compatibility.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 finalized from initial pool after reflection; further self-iteration unlikely to yield better candidates without external tools.

history.rationale: Position 155 is in the antigenic site of HA. Replacing arginine with lysine may alter surface charge and antibody recognition without disrupting core folding.

Position 155 lies in a surface-exposed loop of the HA1 globular head domain; substitution to lysine maintains positive charge and size while potentially altering epitope recognition for antibody escape.
Glycine at 156 is surface-exposed in the head domain. Introducing aspartic acid could modify electrostatic interactions with antibodies while preserving overall structure.
Adjacent to R155; glycine-to-aspartate introduces a charged residue that could sterically hinder antibody binding while the small-to-large change is tolerated in non-core positions.
Serine 158 lies in a variable loop region targeted by antibodies. Asparagine substitution may enhance escape by changing glycosylation potential or side-chain interactions.
Adjacent to 158, this serine change to asparagine is expected to similarly affect antibody binding epitopes while maintaining protein viability.
Valine 189 is part of the Ca1 antigenic site. Alanine substitution can subtly alter hydrophobicity and epitope presentation for immune escape.
Leucine 190 in the Sb site. Proline introduction may rigidify the loop for better antibody evasion, assuming minimal impact on folding stability.
Arginine 225 is in the receptor-binding domain with antigenic relevance. Lysine change could modify charge-based interactions with antibodies.
Arg225 is in the 130-loop region critical for receptor binding; lysine substitution preserves charge and is known to modulate antigenic sites without compromising HA folding stability.
Phenylalanine 226 in antigenic site. Serine substitution reduces side-chain bulk, potentially improving escape while retaining replication fitness.
Threonine 227 at the edge of the antigenic region. Alanine change may fine-tune epitope accessibility for antibody escape.
Proline 228 in the head domain. Serine replacement could adjust conformational flexibility for enhanced immune evasion without compromising viability.
